full_judgment:
Shahabuddin Ahmed CJ: Accused-petitioner is seeking leave to appeal from an order of the High Court Division, dated 12 June 1994 in Criminal Misc. Case No. 749 of 1994, refusing to quash a criminal proceeding under section 561A of the Criminal Procedure Code. 

 2. Respondent No.1, complainant of the Criminal Misc. Case, namely CR No. 210 of 1993, was married to the accused-petitioner in 1984. The allegation of demanding dowry of Tab 50,000.00 was made in 1992; the trial Court, namely, the Thana Magistrate, Patuakhali framed charges against him under the Dowry Prohibition Act. Contention of the petitioner is that the alleged act of demanding dowry does not constitute any offence within the meaning of section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act as this demand even if made is not in consideration of the marriage. But it appears from the complaint-petition that from the very beginning of the marriage demands for money were being made and that Taka 50,000 was demanded as a dowry for the last time. Whether this demand constitutes "dowry" can be determined on evidence during trial. The High Court Division also took the view that since no question of lack of jurisdiction has been raised, it is not a fit case for quashing the proceeding. We do not find any error in the High Court Division's judgment.
